thread:
jordan: Hey team — trying to install the private agent into a customer VPC and the installer is failing during model pulls and pip installs. Hits TLS errors for model registry and pypi, plus our telemetry calls are blocked. Can someone share a minimal outbound allowlist (FQDNs + ports) and any SNI/OCSP tips?

maria-support: Sorry you're hitting this. Quick checklist first — is this behind a corporate proxy that does TLS intercept? If yes, you need SNI passthrough or the proxy's root cert installed in the node's truststore.

jordan: No corporate proxy, it's a managed firewall with egress rules. Example error from installer: `requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: TLSV1_ALERT_UNKNOWN_CA] tlsv1 alert unknown ca (_ssl.c:xxxx)` Also saw curl show: `TLS handshake, certificate signed by unknown authority`.

infra-team: Ok, sounds like either: 1) TLS MITM (proxy/interceptor), or 2) firewall rewrites breaking SNI. Two quick repros: 
- curl -v https://registry.model.redwood.ai/health 
- openssl s_client -connect registry.model.redwood.ai:443 -servername registry.model.redwood.ai 
If the cert CN/SAN doesn't match or you see the MITM cert, it's interception.

alex: For allowlist, we typically recommend allowing FQDNs (not IPs) on 443 and letting TLS passthrough. Minimal set we use for on-prem installer: 
- pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org (pip packages), port 443
- registry.model.redwood.ai (model registry API), port 443
- model-shards.s3.amazonaws.com (AWS S3 model shard hosts via redirects; also cdn.s3.amazonaws.com patterns), port 443
- telemetry.redwood.ai (telemetry/metrics), port 443
- auth.redwood.ai and token.redwood.ai (auth/token exchange), port 443
- artifactory.redwood.ai or internal artifact hosts if you're using mirrors, port 443

maria-support: Addendum: some customers need: 
- ocsp.globalsign.com or ocsp.<CA> (OCSP responders) — if your firewall blocks outbound OCSP/CRL, certificate validation can fail.
- crl3.digicert.com (example CRL endpoints for common CAs)
Also allow outbound DNS (udp/53 and tcp/53) and NTP if image pulls are time-sensitive.

oncall-bot: Help article: https://redwood.ai/docs/onprem/egress (internal KB) :books:

jordan: Thanks. Two followups: 1) customer says they allow *.s3.amazonaws.com but the installer still 502s when fetching shards. 2) How strict are we about IP allowlisting vs DNS?

infra-team: S3 can redirect to region-specific endpoints and to CloudFront CDNs with different hostnames. Allowing only *.s3.amazonaws.com isn't sufficient. We recommend allowing by FQDN patterns listed in S3/public docs *and* the CDN domains you see in curl redirects. If they insist on IP allowlist, they must allow all IP ranges for the relevant cloud region (e.g., AWS IP ranges JSON) which is brittle.

maria-support: For the 502s, paste the exact curl -v output. Often it's TLS SNI mismatch: firewall replaces SNI or strips the server_name extension causing backend to return 502/403. Example curl to debug: 
`curl -v --resolve registry.model.redwood.ai:443:54.33.22.11 https://registry.model.redwood.ai/health`
This forces an IP and shows if SNI matters.

alex: Practical allowlist snippet to share with customers: 
`# outbound allowlist (TCP 443)
- registry.model.redwood.ai
- auth.redwood.ai
- token.redwood.ai
- telemetry.redwood.ai
- pypi.org
- files.pythonhosted.org
- model-shards.*.s3.amazonaws.com (allow all s3 endpoints for your region)
# DNS, OCSP, CRL (UDP/TCP 53 + HTTPS for OCSP)
- crl3.digicert.com
- ocsp.globalsign.com
# Optional if using apt packages
- deb.nodesource.com
- archive.ubuntu.com
`

jordan: Copying that to the customer. They asked if we publish a machine-readable list (for automation).

maria-support: We don't publish a single static IP list because cloud-hosted shards and CDNs change. We have a JSON manifest for on-prem installers with hostnames and example patterns — I'll attach internally. For automation, recommend resolving hostnames at deploy time and allowing those FQDNs (or using an egress proxy that supports SNI-based allowlists).

jordan: One more — customer runs strict DPI which re-signs certs. They can't install our root CA. Any workaround?

infra-team: If they can't install the proxy's root into the nodes, the only safe option is to terminate TLS at their proxy and allow the proxy to communicate to the outside with real certs — but that still requires the proxy to support correct SNI and not rewrite Host headers. Otherwise, it's incompatible with mutual TLS expectations.

maria-support: I'll open a support checklist for this customer: steps we've discussed, reproducible curl/openssl commands, and a recommended allowlist. cc @alex.

jordan: Awesome, thanks all :thumbsup:
